summary: Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at MSU Institute of Asian and African Studies and under George de Roerich. He held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies, Moscow State University, and the Imperial Academy of Sciences.

Gritli von Mitterwallner was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. She completed her Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Munich, where she served as a professor from 1978 to 1991.

Gu Jiegang worked in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Peking University under Taiyan Zhang and Shih Hu, and held posts at Peking University, Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Guang Xing works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of London and SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy Hugh Barrett. He held posts at the University of Hong Kong and the University of British Columbia.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from circa 1986 to 2006 and as a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2006.
Guankong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and served as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudrun Bühnemann works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Münster, Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner, and Bonn. She held research posts in India and Japan before joining the University of Wisconsin-Madison as a professor in 1992.
Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral degrees at the University of Munich, where she was supervised by Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Gudō Wafu Nishijima was a Buddhist studies figure who studied law at the University of Tokyo and trained under Kodo Sawaki and Renpō Niwa. He lectured at the University of Tokyo and Eastern Institute and founded Dogen Sangha International.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held posts at the University of Peradeniya, attested in 1991 and 2008.

Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics scholar. He earned degrees from the University of London and SOAS, studying under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede, and later served as a professor and dean at the University of Ceylon.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied under Stig Wikander and served in a post at Uppsala University from circa 1978 to 2003.
Gunnar Jarring was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lund University from circa 1926 to 1933 and held a post there from circa 1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, and trained under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. He served as abbot at Mahabodhi Monastery in 2013.

Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University under Kenyu Mitomo. He also studied under Sheng Yen and several Japanese teachers including Hoyo Watanabe, Zensho Kitagawa, and Gyoko Iotani.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He earned degrees from Baring Union Christian College, Kent, Harvard, and Columbia. He taught at Columbia from 1988 to 1999 and held an endowed chair at UC Santa Barbara from 1999 to 2015.

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Leiden University and held posts at Utrecht University from 1924 to 1957 and the University of Amsterdam from 1935 to 1944.

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Richard Burghart, Hla Pe, and John Okell, earning a PhD at SOAS University of London, where he later became a Senior Teaching Fellow.

Gustaf John Ramstedt worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1893 to 1902 and held posts at the University of Helsinki and the University of Tokyo.
